title: How mark schemes work
examples: What is the difference between a mark scheme and an answer key?
Can I use the mark scheme to know what the teacher expects?
How do I know if I understood the marking levels?

explain.say: Today we will learn about mark schemes for exams.

items: Mark schemes show how answers are marked.
They explain what points earn marks.
They help you know what to include.

explain.say: First we look at M marks and A marks.
Next we learn about the levels of response.
Following through means you keep your ideas connected.

items: Idea 1: Start with a clear point.

explain.say: In everyday life, a recipe uses clear steps.
A common mistake is only stating facts without explaining them.

items: You must explain how they connect.

faq.q: What is the difference between a mark scheme and an answer key?
faq.a: An answer key just gives the right answer. A mark scheme explains how many marks you get for different parts of your answer.
asks: Is it the same as a marking guide?
Does it just list correct answers?

faq.q: Do I need to know the mark scheme to pass the exam?
faq.a: No, you do not need to memorize it. But knowing it helps you structure your answers better for better marks.
asks: Should I study the mark scheme?

faq.q: What does 'level of response' mean in my exam?
faq.a: It means how deep your thinking is shown. A higher level shows deeper analysis and connection of ideas.
asks: What is the difference between good and excellent?

faq.a: It means that every point you make should lead logically to the next point. Your ideas must connect smoothly.
asks: How do I make my ideas flow?
Does it mean using transition words?

faq.q: Can I use the mark scheme when I write my actual exam?
faq.a: No, you cannot use it during the exam. You must use the knowledge it taught you to write your own answer.
asks: Is it allowed in the exam hall?
Can I look at it while writing?

facts: Mark schemes break down how marks are awarded.
M marks relate to main concepts or points.
A marks reward accurate development of those points.
Follow-through shows logical connection between ideas.

quiz.say: When writing about the causes of World War One, which structure shows the best 'follow-through'?

options.show: Starting and ending with a summary.
options.say: Starting and ending with a summary.

options.show: Point A leads to Explanation B, which proves Conclusion C.
options.say: Point A leads to Explanation B, which proves Conclusion C.

options.show: Only providing evidence for each point.
options.say: Only providing evidence for each point.

quiz.why: Following through means your points build on each other logically, like a chain.

wrong.0: While summaries are good, they do not guarantee the connection between the body paragraphs.
wrong.2: This shows three ideas, but it does not show how one idea leads to the next.
wrong.3: Evidence is good, but without a connecting idea, it feels like separate facts.

quiz.say: A student writes: 'The river flows fast. It erodes the bank. This creates a gorge.' This demonstrates:
quiz.why: The sentence structure shows a clear cause and effect chain from one idea to the next.

wrong.1: This shows more than just the main points; it shows the process too.
wrong.2: The connection shows a higher level of understanding than just basic facts.
wrong.3: The use of 'This creates' links the ideas, which is more than just listing.
